intro: Lesson 65: Reflection and refraction of light. To understand how light reflects and refracts, and how to draw accurate ray diagrams

picture.alt: A light ray refracting through a glass block
picture.draw: Draw and label: Ray diagram sheet

model.title: A ray hits a plane mirror at 35° to the mirror surface. Find the angle of reflection.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Angle to the surface is not the angle of incidence

questions.q: A ray enters water at 30° to the normal and refracts to 22°. Explain why it bent.
questions.a: Light slows down in water (1), so it changes direction towards the normal (1)
questions.model: What changed? The medium. What happens to speed? It slows. Slower, so it bends towards the normal: 30° became 22°.

questions.q: What angle of refraction occurs when i = 0°?

questions.a: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection

questions.q: Draw a ray entering and leaving a rectangular glass block at i = 40° (use the data: r = 25°) [4], and explain the emergent ray's direction [2].
questions.a: Normal at each face, refraction towards normal entering, away leaving (4); emergent ray parallel to incident ray because the faces are parallel and the bending is reversed (2)
questions.model: Teacher draws the block, the first normal and the incident ray on screen.

questions.q: Explain why a straw in a glass of water looks bent.
questions.a: Light from the straw refracts at the water surface (1), bending away from the normal into air (1); the brain traces rays back in straight lines, so the straw appears displaced (1)

questions.q: Why do waves refract when they slow down? Use wavefronts.
questions.a: One side of the wavefront enters the slower medium first and slows, so the wavefront turns.

questions.q: Big question: should you trust a pool's depth by eye?
questions.a: No: refraction makes the bottom look higher than it is.
